title: Mammals
examples: Do all mammals have to live on land?
What is the difference between a mammal and a reptile?
Can we find any animals that are not mammals?

explain.say: Today we are learning about mammals, which are a special group of animals. Say that with me, mammals.
One key thing about mammals is that they are warm-blooded. This means they can keep their own body temperature steady. For example, a dog keeps its body warm even when it is cold outside.
Another important trait is that most mammals have hair or fur covering their bodies. This helps keep them warm and protected. Think about a fluffy cat; it has soft fur all over.
Mammals also feed their young milk, which comes from their mothers. This milk is very nutritious and helps the baby grow strong. A human baby drinks milk from its mother.

Some mammals live in surprising places, like the ocean or the air. Whales are mammals because they breathe air and give live birth. Bats are mammals because they feed their young milk. They show us that mammals are diverse.
In real life, think about a pet dog. It is warm-blooded, it has fur, and it nurses its puppies with milk. These traits show it is a mammal.

faq.q: Do all mammals have to have fur?
faq.a: No, not all mammals have visible fur. Some, like whales, have skin that is smooth, but they still have the other key traits.

faq.q: How do we know if a whale is really a mammal?
faq.a: We know because whales breathe air using lungs, like us. They also give birth to live young and feed them milk.

faq.q: What is the difference between giving birth and laying eggs?
faq.a: Mammals give birth to live young that are already formed. Animals that lay eggs, like birds, hatch their young from an egg.

faq.q: Are bats mammals even though they fly?
faq.a: Yes, bats are mammals because they possess the defining traits: they are warm-blooded, they have hair, and they feed their young milk.
asks: What makes a bat a mammal?

faq.q: What does 'warm-blooded' actually mean for an animal?
faq.a: It means the animal can generate and maintain a constant internal body temperature without relying on the outside environment.
asks: What is the meaning of warm-blooded?
How do mammals control their temperature?

facts: Mammals are characterized by having hair or fur.
They are warm-blooded, meaning their body temperature stays constant.
All mammals feed their young milk produced by the mother.
Whales are mammals because they breathe air and nurse their young.
